item.title: 1: Even HaEzer Siman 1: The Obligation of Marriage
item.description:
Where does the obligation to marry come from? The Torah never states it directly, but Peru Urevu, the first misvah, requires children and marriage is the way to have them. The Shulhan Arukh and Mishnah apply this obligation to men, and the Gemara calls the unmarried man incomplete.

item.title: 2: Even HaEzer Siman 1: The Misvah of Having Children Part 1
item.description:
Peru Urevu falls on men, fulfilled through marriage, and there is also an independent misvah to be married, from the verse that it is not good for man to be alone. According to Rav Moshe Feinstein, the misvah lies in trying to have children, not the result.

item.title: 4: Even HaEzer Siman 1: The Misvah of Having Children Part 3: IVF
item.description:

item.title: 5: Even HaEzer Siman 1: The Misvah of Having Children Part 4: Age of Marriage 1
item.description:
At what age does the misvah of having children begin? Although a boy takes on misvot at thirteen, the Mishnah gives eighteen for marriage, which the Rambam reads as the start of the eighteenth year, seventeen. The shiur gives reasons, including Torah study, and notes the Rambam and Shulhan Arukh say by twenty.

item.description:

item.title: 8: Even HaEzer Siman 1: The Misvah of Having Children Part 7: Age of Marriage for Women

item.title: 11: Even HaEzer Siman 1: The Misvah of Having Children Part 10: Selling a Torah for Marriage
item.description:
Can a Sefer Torah be sold for marriage? Three components of the misvah of marriage are reviewed: marriage itself, Peru Urevu and Shevet. The Gemara forbids selling a Sefer Torah, but permits it to enable marriage and children, because the Torah exists to be learned. Many Rishonim extend this to a woman's marrying.

item.title: 13: Even HaEzer Siman 1: The Misvah of Having Children Part 12: Introduction to Contraception
item.description:
When may a couple use contraception despite the misvah of having children? item.description:
